items.excerpt: LTX released LTX-2.5, an open-weights video world model studios can run on their own hardware, keeping IP and prompts in-house. It handles ACES HDR end to end and renders multishot sequences as a single output; available now via Hugging Face, the LTX API and ComfyUI.

Adobe made three Firefly AI audio tools generally available, letting editors generate music, voiceover and custom sound effects without leaving the app, with all generated music licensed for commercial use. Note: adjacent to the 8/21 Firefly card (postPerspective) — treat as possible dupe of that story.
items.dupe_risk: Same Firefly release family as the card published 2026-08-21; different outlet and audio-specific angle.

items.excerpt: Reallusion launched AccuFACE 2, an AI-driven markerless facial mocap system aimed at production-grade performance capture for CC5 HD characters from ordinary webcam or iPhone capture. It targets small teams doing character animation without a mocap stage.

Profuz Digital's SubtitleNext adds expanded AI transcription integrations with AssemblyAI, Deepgram, ElevenLabs and Whisper, plus IMSCR support and batch processing for subtitle and audio-description work. It points at AI moving into routine localization pipelines rather than hero shots.

A new in-depth report goes inside Studio Ghibli as it confronts its next film, Miyazaki's succession and its stance on AI — separating the tool from how it's used. It's a rare, concrete read on how a craft-first studio frames generative tech.

The Motion Picture Association signed a memorandum of understanding with ByteDance to block studio IP from being reproduced by its Seedance/Seedream generative video models. It effectively sets guardrails on what one of the most-used AI video tools will let creators generate. Same story also covered by Engadget (engadget.com/2238384) if a different outlet is preferred.

Filmmaker and AI executive Verena Puhm launched Matriarch, a production company building animation and documentary projects around hybrid human/AI pipelines. Lower priority: closer to a company-launch story than a craft or tooling shift.

A filmmaker recovered a lost 1971 Billy Joel radio interview and used AI to re-create the young singer on screen around the real audio. '1971: Billy Joel's Lost Interview' is a working test case for AI reconstruction in documentary — and the disclosure questions it raises.

Roku launched Fairground AI, a 24/7 free channel programmed entirely with AI-generated narrative shorts and commercials. It's the first mainstream US distribution slot built purely for synthetic video, and a live read on whether audiences will sit with it.

'Castle Walls,' an AI-generated Turkish short-form series, launched on Prime Video in what's billed as the first fully AI show to premiere worldwide on a major streamer. It marks the shift from AI festival shorts to platform-distributed series.

LA VFX studio Impossible Objects details running custom AI models locally on HP ZGX Nano workstations, blending generative passes with traditional VFX while keeping client assets off the cloud. A concrete look at hybrid, on-prem AI in a working commercial pipeline.
